title: Division
description: Class 2 IMO — Division as equal sharing and equal grouping, the link with multiplication, and simple word problems for the Maths Olympiad.

topics.title: Division as Equal Sharing
topics.concept: Division means sharing equally. If 12 sweets are shared among 3 children, each child gets 12 ÷ 3 = 4 sweets. The sign ÷ means divided by. Sharing equally means every group gets the same amount.
recap: Division shares things into equal groups.

quiz.q: Share 8 balloons between 2 children. Each gets ___ ?

topics.title: Division as Equal Grouping
topics.concept: Division also tells how many equal groups we can make. If we have 12 oranges and put 4 in each bag, we make 12 ÷ 4 = 3 bags. Here we know how many in each group and find the number of groups.

examples.problem: 18 students sit 2 to a bench. How many benches?

recap: Division can find the number of equal groups.
Total ÷ size of each group = number of groups.

quiz.q: How many groups of 3 can be made from 12?

topics.title: Multiplication–Division Link & Word Problems
topics.concept: Division is the opposite of multiplication. Since 4 × 5 = 20, we know 20 ÷ 5 = 4 and 20 ÷ 4 = 5. In word problems, words like share equally, each and how many groups mean divide.

examples.problem: 24 laddoos shared equally among 4 plates. How many per plate?

recap: 'Share equally / each / how many groups' means divide.

quiz.q: 16 chocolates are shared equally among 4 children. Each gets ___ ?

questions.q: Which is the odd one out (three equal 5):  10 ÷ 2, 15 ÷ 3, 25 ÷ 5, 20 ÷ 5?
Sharing is to division as joining equal groups is to ___ ?
questions.explanation: Equal groups joined together is multiplication.

questions.q: How many groups of 2 are there in 18?
12 bananas are shared equally among 3 monkeys. Each monkey gets ___ ?
20 students form teams of 5. How many teams?
₹50 is shared equally between 5 children. How much does each get?
A teacher has 24 sweets. She gives 4 sweets to each child. How many children get sweets?
There are 18 eggs. They are packed into trays of 6. How many full trays, and how many eggs are left over?
questions.explanation: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 trays exactly, with none left over.
